data.title: Icon, checks on PRs, refactoring of expenses and AGENTS.md

events.goal: Fix the remaining remarks from the report
requirements: When everything is ready, open a PR and merge it

events.line: Accepted, I will study the code and write the statement for the remaining remarks
events.text:
Write a task for the split-bill project. The app "Split the bill" is ready: Vite with a relative base path, TypeScript strict, Vitest, ESLint, Prettier, vanilla DOM, checks through make check (types, linter, tests, build), formatting through npm run format. The site is deployed to GitHub Pages by a workflow on push to main: install dependencies, make check, deployment.

The human's task: fix the remaining remarks from the report. First: there is no site icon, the browser requests favicon.ico and gets 404, on Pages too. Second: the checks run only on push to main, there are none on a pull request. Third: formatting is not part of the checks, neither make check nor CI catches unformatted code. Fourth: in the expenses section file the function that creates the section is long, about 155 lines, it contains both building the form and handlers and redrawing; in the description of an expense inside a ternary operator there is a template string with a chain of map and join, which breaks the rule "an intermediate result gets a name"; earlier the review also noted that the redraw mixes levels of abstraction. Fifth: the constant of kopecks in a ruble is exported but probably used nowhere, check.

The human's decisions: he does not wait for the statement to be approved, choose a simple, reliable and clear option, write the section "Accepted decisions" instead of questions. The icon: without new dependencies, a simple SVG on the theme, works with a relative base path and from a subdirectory; the criterion — no 404 on the icon in the check from a subdirectory and the browser does not request favicon.ico. Formatting: add a check script and a Makefile target included in make check, the cheap checks first; make sure generated files and the journal are ignored and that the current tree passes the check; take into account that the checks are run by both the stop hook and CI. CI on PRs: a separate workflow "Checks" on pull request into main with Node 22 and the npm cache, installing dependencies and make check, read-only permissions and cancelling the previous run of the same branch; the action versions as in the deployment; think about whether to extract the shared steps, but decide by the principle of simplicity and write the decision down; in the README add a line about the checks on PRs. The expenses section: split into functions of one action each — building the form, reading and checking, the expense row, redrawing — without changing the behavior and markup, with named intermediate results and nesting no deeper than two; the previous DOM tests must pass without changing the expectations. Remove the kopecks constant from the exports if it is not used outside.

Follow the project rules. Specify how to split the work into small coherent commits by the remarks. Anything else noticed goes to "Out of scope".

events.line: Here is the statement: icon, format in the checks, CI on PRs, refactoring
events.text:
The statement is ready. Goal: close the remaining remarks. The site gets an icon and the requests answered with 404 disappear, make check and CI start to check formatting, the checks run on a pull request into main, and the expenses section file and the money file are brought to the project rules. The behavior of the app does not change.

A plan of five commits, after each make check is green.

First: the constant of kopecks in a ruble is no longer exported, it is needed only inside the function that shows rubles, nobody uses it outside.

Second: the expenses section is split into functions of one action each without changing the markup, texts, attributes and behavior. Building the form is moved into a separate function with a description of the form fields, reading and checking the form return either an expense or an error, and the branching by the result is exhaustive. Submitting the form only names the steps: read the form, add the expense, check the sum limit, reset the form, change the bill. Filling the payer list and the recipient checkboxes is split into two actions. The description of the recipients is moved into a separate function: this way the chain of map and join inside the ternary operator and the template string disappears. The redraw only names the steps. Nesting no deeper than two levels, no new files.

Third: the site icon as an SVG file in the public directory, a coin split in half, in the colors from the styles, without external links and fonts; in index.html a link to it before the heading. Checked in a copy of the project: with a relative base path Vite rewrites the link and copies the file into the build, from the deployment subdirectory the file answers 200 with the type image/svg+xml.

Fourth: a formatting check script, a Makefile target that stands first in make check as the cheapest, and a line in the README. The Prettier ignore file does not change: the generated files and the journal are already in it, the current tree passes the check.

Fifth: the workflow "Checks" on pull request into main with read-only permissions, cancelling the previous run of the same branch, installing Node 22 with the npm cache, installing dependencies and make check; the action versions are the same as in the deployment. The README is extended with lines about the checks on PRs.

Accepted decisions. The icon lies as a file in the public directory, not as a data URI: this is simpler to read and edit, and Vite itself makes the link relative. We do not introduce a reusable workflow: only the installation of three steps is shared, and the checks themselves are already described in one place, in make check; extracting the installation would require passing the deployment artifact through a called workflow, and there would be more complexity than duplication. The Makefile target is called format-check, the script is format:check. The cancellation group is taken by the branch of the pull request. The ignore file does not need to be changed, the stop hook will not fail on the files that it writes itself.

Done criteria: make check is green and checks formatting as the first step, with a broken indent it fails; the formatting check passes; the constant export is removed; all tests pass without changing the expectations; in the expenses section there is no map and join inside a template or a ternary operator, nesting is no deeper than two, the redraw only calls named steps; the build has a link to the icon and the icon file, from a subdirectory it is served with 200; the workflow triggers on pull request into main with the needed permissions and cancellation; the README reflects everything said.

New tests are not needed: the refactoring is fixed by the existing DOM tests.

Out of scope: refactoring of other interface sections, the sections "Code and tests" and "Tasks" in AGENTS.md, merging the workflows, favicon.ico, the icon for Apple devices and the manifest. About AGENTS.md I will note to the human: it says that the domain logic lies in two directories, while ESLint and the README also attribute the sharing directory to it, so the file lags a little behind the code; the section "Tasks" is empty.

events.line: Accepted. I do five steps, I do not commit, fixes by files separately
events.text:

The human's task: fix the remaining remarks from the report. Goal: the site gets an icon, make check and CI check formatting, the checks run on a pull request into main, the expenses section file and the money file are brought to the project rules; the behavior of the app does not change.

Step 1: remove the export of the kopecks-in-a-ruble constant, check that it is not used outside. Step 2: refactor the expenses section without changing the markup, texts, attributes and behavior. Building the form in a separate function with the type of fields, reading and checking the form return an expense or an error with exhaustive branching, submitting the form only names the steps, the payer list and the recipient checkboxes are filled by two functions, the description of the recipients is extracted so that there is no chain inside a template or a ternary operator, while the logic "for everyone" stays the same; the redraw only calls named steps; nesting no deeper than two, no new files. Step 3: an icon as an SVG file with a coin split in half, in the colors from the styles, without external links; a link to it in index.html before the heading; do not touch the Vite config. Step 4: a formatting check script, the Makefile target first in make check, a line in the README about the checks; do not change the Prettier ignore file. Step 5: the workflow "Checks" on pull request into main with read permissions, cancelling the previous run of the branch, Node 22 with the npm cache, installing dependencies and make check, the action versions as in the deployment; do not change the deployment; the README is extended with lines about the checks on PRs; at the end run the formatting.

Done criteria: make check is green and checks formatting as the first step, with a broken indent in a copy it fails; the formatting check passes; the constant export is removed; all tests pass without changing the expectations; in the expenses section there is no map and join inside a template or a ternary operator, nesting is no deeper than two; the build has a relative link to the icon and the icon file, from a subdirectory it is served with the code 200; the workflow parses as YAML; the README reflects the formatting check and the checks on PRs. New tests are not needed. Out of scope: other sections, the project rules, merging the workflows, favicon.ico, the icon for Apple devices, the manifest.

At the end run the layout check script from the temporary directory: it builds the app and checks it from a subdirectory, including failed requests. Then the formatting and make check, it must be green. In the answer write what was done by steps, deviations and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here you are. All five steps are done, make check and the layout are green
events.text:
All five steps are done. Formatting and make check are green, the layout check passed at 360, 768 and 1280 px, including failed requests. I did not commit anything. I did not change tests and did not add new ones: 285 tests pass.

Step 1. The kopecks-in-a-ruble constant lost its export: it was not used outside the file, a search of the sources confirmed this.

Step 2. The expenses section is refactored by the plan, the markup, texts, attributes and behavior are the same. Appeared are the description of the form fields and the type of the reading result, the functions of building the form, getting and marking the checkboxes, reading the form, resetting the form, filling the payer list, creating and filling the recipient checkboxes, describing the recipients and the expense, creating the expense row and redrawing it, clearing the message and showing the form when there are participants. The logic "for everyone" is the same as before: the number of recipients is compared with the number of participants. The branching by the reading result goes through a check of the error field. Submitting the form only names the steps, the redraw only calls named steps, and the argument of the row replacement is taken from a variable. The function that creates the section contains building the section, subscribing to submit, the state of the rendered participants with the former comment, the submit, the redraw and the return.

Step 3. A new icon file: a coin split in half, the left half dark, the right one green, a white background, without external links. In index.html a link to the icon is added before the heading. After the build the link became relative, the icon file lies in the build. I did not run the check by a request from a subdirectory by hand: instead the layout check script passed, which checks the app from a subdirectory and catches failed requests.

Step 4. A formatting check script is added, the Makefile target is added to the list of targets and stands first in make check, the line in the README now says "checks: formatting, types, linter, tests, build". I checked on a copy: after breaking the indent in the expenses section file make check fails on the formatting check with a non-zero code.

Step 5. The new workflow "Checks" is made by the description, the YAML parses, I did not change the deployment. In the README the line about the workflows is now "checks on pull request and deployment to GitHub Pages", and in the section about the deployment it is added that the workflow "Checks" runs make check on every pull request into main. The README fixes of steps 4 and 5 lie in one file, as you warned.

There are no deviations, nothing noticed on the way outside the task either. New files: the icon and the checks workflow.

Third: the site icon in an SVG file, a coin in half in the colors from the styles, a link in index.html; with a relative base path Vite makes the link relative. Fourth: a formatting check script, the Makefile target first in make check, a line in the README. Fifth: the workflow "Checks" on pull request into main with read permissions, cancelling the previous run of the branch, Node 22 with the npm cache, installing dependencies and make check; the README is extended. The decisions of the statement: the icon as a file, not a data URI; we do not introduce a reusable workflow, because only the installation is shared, and the checks themselves are already in one place.

Done criteria: make check is green and checks formatting as the first step, with a broken indent in a copy it fails; the formatting check passes; the constant export is removed; all tests pass without changing the expectations, the test files were not changed; in the expenses section there is no chain of map and join inside a template or a ternary operator, nesting is no deeper than two, the redraw only calls named steps; the build has a relative link to the icon and the icon file, from a subdirectory it is served with the code 200, check it yourself; the workflow is as described, the YAML is correct, the action versions exist; the README reflects the formatting check and the checks on PRs.

Check especially that the refactoring does not change the behavior: keeping the payer on redraw, resetting the checkboxes when the participants change, the form errors, the sum limit, the captions of the delete buttons — compare with the previous version by the difference. Check the project rules: names, one function — one action, levels of abstraction, names of intermediate results. Check that the SVG has no external links and scripts and that the formatting check will not break the Cyberzavod stop hook: the journal is ignored.

events.line: Accepted, the criteria are met, there are three readability nitpicks
events.text:
ACCEPTED. All the done criteria are met, there are no serious remarks. Below are three readability nitpicks, fixing them is not mandatory.

What I checked. make check is green, the first step is the formatting check, then types, linter, 285 tests and the build; in a copy I broke the indent in the expenses section file, and make check returned a non-zero code pointing at that file. The formatting check passes. A search for the export of the kopecks constant is empty, it is still used by the function that shows rubles in the same file. The test files were not changed: the difference has only the Makefile, README, index.html, package.json, the money file and the expenses section. In the expenses section the chain of map and join is no longer inside a template: in the description of the recipients there is first the early exit "for everyone", then a variable with the names; nesting is no deeper than two; the types and all functions from the task are in place. The build has a relative link to the icon, the icon file is there; I copied the build into a subdirectory, started a static server, and the icon is served with the code 200 and the type image/svg+xml. The SVG has no external links, scripts or event handlers, and the colors match the styles. The checks workflow parses as YAML, everything is as in the description, the tags of the action versions exist and match the deployment. The README is updated in both places. The stop hook will not suffer: the ignore file excludes the journal, the Cyberzavod and Claude directories, the project rules, the build and the coverage; in the docs directory there is only a picture, and Prettier does not check SVG.

I compared the behavior of the refactoring with the previous version by the difference, it did not change. Submitting the form: the order of checks is the same — amount, recipients, total limit; the identifier is created only for a valid expense; resetting the amount and marking all recipients happen after the limit check, before the change of the bill. The redraw: clearing the message, showing the form or the hint, the payers and checkboxes only on a new reference to the participant list, the expense rows; the payer is kept if still among the participants; when the participants change the checkboxes are created anew and marked. The markup, the captions of the delete buttons, the texts and the order of elements are the same. These scenarios are covered by DOM tests.

Nitpicks. First: in the redraw the condition of the participant list change did not get a name, and after the multiline block there is no blank line before redrawing the expense rows; these are two project rules, and the criterion "the redraw only calls steps" is not fully met, because it still has a comparison and a state write. Second: in submitting the form the message is written by hand, although there is a separate function for clearing; a symmetric function of showing the message would remove the mixing of levels. Third: the function of filling the payers takes only the select list, and the neighboring checkbox function takes the whole form; the signatures of neighboring steps are inconsistent.

There are no secrets, server addresses or personal data in the changes. There is no new logic without a test: the changes are a refactoring and settings, the existing tests cover them.

events.line: Accepted. I fix the three nitpicks from the review in the expenses section
events.text:
Make three small fixes in the uncommitted refactoring of the expenses section. The review accepted the task, these fixes bring the refactoring up to the project rules. The behavior, markup and texts do not change, do not touch tests, do not commit, do not change other files.

First: in the redraw the condition of the participant list change gets a name, for example about the participants having changed, and after the multiline if block a blank line is put before the redraw of the expense rows.

Second: in submitting the form the message is written by hand, while there is a separate function for clearing. Introduce a symmetric module function of showing a message with a form and a text and use it, so that the submit only names the steps.

Third: make the signatures of neighboring steps consistent. Filling the payers takes only the select list, while filling the recipient checkboxes takes the whole form. Make them the same, for example both take the form.

Then the formatting and make check, it must be green. The answer is two or three lines.

events.line: Here you are. Three nitpicks fixed, make check is green
events.text:

The git status has other changed files too: the Makefile, README, index.html, package.json, the money file, the checks workflow and the public directory. These are not my fixes, I did not touch them.

events.line: Checks passed, I added four tests for the form edge cases
events.text:
CHECKS PASSED.

First: make check is green: the formatting check, types, linter, 289 tests, the build. The first step in the Makefile is the formatting check; I broke the indent in the main file of the app, and make check returned a non-zero code, after which I restored the file. Second: the formatting check passes and is part of make check. Third: there is no export of the kopecks-in-a-ruble constant. Fourth: all tests pass, the existing expectations did not change, in the DOM tests only 48 lines were added and none removed, the other test files are not touched. Fifth: by reading the expenses section I checked that inside template strings and ternaries there is no chain of map and join, join is moved into the description of the recipients in a separate variable, nesting is no more than two levels, and the redraw calls only named steps. Sixth: in the build the link to the icon is relative, the icon file is in place, from a subdirectory it is served with the code 200 and the type image/svg+xml. Seventh: there is no favicon.ico request, no failed requests, the page, the styles and the script were served with 200. Headless Chromium did not request the icon itself, so I did not see the request for the SVG; instead I read the address from the icon link and loaded it on the page, the code was 200. Only this remains unchecked: that a real browser will request the icon itself. I used my own script, not the shared layout check script. Eighth: the checks workflow parses as YAML and contains what is needed: pull request on main, read permissions, cancelling the previous run, checkout and setup-node of version 7 with Node 22 and the npm cache, installing dependencies and make check. Ninth: in the README the line about make check says "formatting", and the checks on PRs are written in the section about the structure and in the section about the deployment.

The edge cases of the refactoring. I added four tests to the DOM tests of the app, all pass: the payer is kept after adding a participant; after removing the chosen payer who has no expenses, Ann is chosen, and the expense is added for her; an amount error, then a fix — the expense is added, the message is empty; exceeding the sum limit leaves the entered amount and the unchecked recipient checkbox in the form. The existing test about rejecting an expense on exceeding the limit already checks that the expense list and the address do not change.

The code is formatted. I changed only the DOM test file of the app.

events.line: All remarks are closed, five commits pushed, merge the PR?
events.text:

By the way, the analyst noticed that AGENTS.md lags a little behind the code. The section "Code and tests" does not mention src/sharing, although it is also without the DOM, and ESLint enforces this. The section "Tasks" is empty. I did not touch this.

Open a PR and merge it? At the same time the new workflow "Checks" will run for the first time on it.

events.line: Accepted. I will add src/sharing and the section about tasks to AGENTS.md
events.text:
Update the rules of the split-bill project, that is AGENTS.md. Do not change other files, do not commit. Do not edit by hand the files generated by the harness sync.

The human's task: update AGENTS.md, adding src/sharing and a section about tasks.

First. In the section "Code and tests", in the first item, it now says that the domain logic lies in src/bill and src/settlement. Add src/sharing: encoding the bill into a link is also without the DOM, ESLint enforces this, check in its config. A wording, for example: the domain logic lies in src/bill, src/settlement and src/sharing and does not know about the DOM, ESLint enforces this; the interface is in src/ui.

Second. In the section "Tasks" leave the intro line, as the intro is left in "Code and tests", and add items by the human's decision. Tasks are issues of the GitHub repository, a task is read in full by its number: the description and the comments. A task can also be given as text in a session — then the commits carry no reference. A commit that closes a task from an issue writes Closes #N in the body, so that the issue is closed when it is merged into main. Write briefly, in the style of the other items of the file, in Russian.

After the fix check whether the generated files are stale with the sync command with the check, and run make check. If the sync reports that the files are stale, run it and report which files it changed. In the answer write the final text of the two sections and the results of the commands.

events.line: Here is the report: AGENTS.md is updated, check is green
events.text:
AGENTS.md is updated, in the working tree only it is changed. Nothing is committed.

ESLint already enforces src/sharing: in its config this directory stands in the list together with src/bill and src/settlement. The directory src/sharing exists.

The final text of the two sections. The section "Tasks": the intro line "Where tasks live, how to read them and how to reference them in commits." and three items. Tasks are issues of the GitHub repository, a task is read in full by its number: the description and the comments. A task can also be given as text in a session — then the commits carry no reference. A commit that closes a task from an issue writes Closes #N in the body, so that the issue is closed when it is merged into main.

The section "Code and tests": the intro line "Rules for code and tests of the project: the implementer writes by them, the tester and the reviewer check against them." and three items. The domain logic lies in src/bill, src/settlement and src/sharing and does not know about the DOM: ESLint enforces this; the interface is in src/ui. Tests lie next to the code as files with the suffix test.ts, DOM tests are marked with a comment about the jsdom environment. Amounts are stored in kopecks as integers, they are turned into rubles only on input and on display.

The results of the commands. The sync with the check: exit code 0, no output, the generated files are not stale, so the sync itself was not run and the generated files did not change. make check: exit code 0, the linter is clean, the tests passed (10 files, 289 tests), the build passed.
